title: Treasury Bills (T-Bills)
subtitle: Short-term sovereign cash management instruments (91, 182, and 364 days)
summary: Treasury Bills are short-term zero-coupon debt obligations issued by the Government of India at a discount, offering sovereign safety for parking cash over months.

sources.name: Reserve Bank of India - Treasury Bill Auctions Guidelines
RBI Retail Direct Treasury Bills Portal

sections.title: What are Treasury Bills?
sections.content: Treasury Bills (T-Bills) are short-term promissory notes issued by the Government of India through RBI auctions to bridge short-term cash flow gaps. They carry maturities of 91 days, 182 days, or 364 days.
sections.analogy: Imagine buying a government gift certificate worth ₹100 for ₹93.50 today. In one year, the government gives you the full ₹100. The ₹6.50 difference is your earnings. T-Bills pay no ongoing coupon—the profit is embedded in the discount price.

sections.title: How Investors Earn from T-Bills
points: Issued at a discount to the face value of ₹100.
Redeemed at 100% of par face value upon maturity date.
The difference between the discounted purchase price and redemption price represents the return.

sections.title: What are the Risks?
sections.content: T-Bills are among the lowest-risk financial assets in the Indian currency system:
points: Reinvestment Risk: Because maturities are under 1 year, when the bill matures you must reinvest at whatever interest rates prevail in the future.
Inflation Risk: Short-term cash yields may trail high food/energy inflation spikes.
Credit Risk: Backed by the sovereign; credit default risk is negligible in INR.

sections.title: Who Often Considers T-Bills?
sections.content: Individuals and businesses wanting an alternative to bank savings accounts or short-term fixed deposits for emergency funds, upcoming tax outlays, or capital waiting to be deployed.

sections.title: Worked Example (Sample Illustration)
sections.content: An investor bids for a 364-day T-Bill in a weekly RBI auction.
details: Cut-off price determined in auction: ₹93.65 per unit (face value ₹100).
After 364 days, RBI deposits ₹1,00,000 directly into the investor's bank account.

sections.title: Tax Overview in Plain English
points: Under Indian tax provisions, the discount earned on T-Bills upon maturity is treated as short-term capital gain (or other income) and taxed at the individual's marginal slab rate.
There is no TDS on redemption payments via RBI Retail Direct.

sections.title: How to Buy T-Bills
steps: Via RBI Retail Direct: Place non-competitive bids on Wednesdays for 91-day, 182-day, or 364-day bills with minimum ₹10,000.
Via Stockbroker Apps: Most modern retail brokers (Zerodha, Groww, Upstox, etc.) offer a dedicated Government Bonds & T-Bills window during weekly bidding cycles.

items.myth: T-Bills pay monthly or quarterly interest.
items.fact: T-Bills are zero-coupon instruments. All returns are paid upon maturity when the bill is redeemed at par.

items.myth: There are penalty lock-ins if you need money back.
items.fact: T-Bills are credited to Demat/CSGL accounts and can be traded on secondary exchange debt segments before maturity.

terms.definition: A debt instrument that does not pay periodic interest coupons but trades at a deep discount to face value.
The price determined in RBI auctions at which all successful non-competitive bidders receive allotment.
